questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Continuous Integration (CI)?
questions.option_a: To automatically deploy every code change directly to production
questions.option_b: To frequently integrate code changes into a shared repository and automatically build and test the application
questions.option_c: To replace software developers with automated testing tools
questions.option_d: To perform security testing only after an application is deployed
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration involves frequently integrating code changes into a shared repository and automatically building and testing the application.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes Continuous Delivery?
questions.option_a: Validated software is automatically deployed to production without human intervention
questions.option_b: Software is prepared and validated so that it is ready for release
questions.option_c: Developers manually compile applications without automated testing
questions.option_d: Security testing is performed exclusively after deployment
questions.explanation: Continuous Delivery prepares validated software for release. Actual production deployment may still require manual approval.

questions.question: What distinguishes Continuous Deployment from Continuous Delivery?
questions.option_a: Continuous Deployment automatically deploys validated changes to production
questions.option_b: Continuous Deployment eliminates the need for automated testing
questions.option_c: Continuous Delivery always deploys directly to production
questions.option_d: Continuous Deployment only performs source-code compilation
questions.explanation: Continuous Deployment automatically deploys validated changes to production, whereas Continuous Delivery prepares software for release.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a typical CI activity in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Unit testing
questions.option_b: Integration testing
questions.option_d: Manually approving every production deployment
questions.explanation: CI includes activities such as compilation, unit testing, integration testing, code quality analysis, and security scanning. Manual deployment approval is not a defining CI activity.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents the typical CI/CD pipeline presented in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Developer → Git Repository → Build → Test → Security Checks → Package → Deploy → Production
questions.option_b: Developer → Production → Build → Test → Git Repository → Deploy
questions.option_c: Git Repository → Production → Security Checks → Developer → Build
questions.option_d: Developer → Deploy → Test → Build → Security Checks → Production
questions.explanation: The lecture presents a pipeline beginning with developer code changes and repository integration, followed by building, testing, security checks, packaging, and deployment.

questions.question: Why is integrating security into CI/CD preferable to traditional late-stage security testing?
questions.option_a: It eliminates all software vulnerabilities
questions.option_b: It identifies vulnerabilities earlier, reducing remediation costs and providing faster feedback
questions.option_c: It removes the need for developers to review their code
questions.option_d: It ensures that every application is automatically compliant with all regulations
questions.explanation: Integrating security throughout CI/CD enables earlier vulnerability detection, faster feedback, and lower remediation costs.

questions.question: What does Shift-Left Security mean?
questions.option_a: Moving security activities toward the end of the deployment process
questions.option_b: Moving security activities earlier in the software development lifecycle
questions.option_c: Moving all security responsibilities to a separate security team
questions.option_d: Performing security testing only on production systems
questions.explanation: Shift-Left Security means incorporating security activities earlier in the software development lifecycle rather than waiting until the final stages.

questions.question: A developer introduces a third-party dependency containing a known vulnerability. Which approach best demonstrates Shift-Left Security?
questions.option_a: Wait until customers report exploitation
questions.option_b: Perform a dependency scan immediately after the dependency is introduced
questions.option_c: Wait until the application reaches production
questions.option_d: Remove all automated testing from the pipeline
questions.explanation: An early SCA scan identifies vulnerable dependencies before they progress further through the development lifecycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of security automation in CI/CD?
questions.option_a: Increased dependence on manual security reviews
questions.option_b: Reduced consistency between builds
questions.option_c: Reduced human error through automated and repeatable security checks
questions.option_d: Elimination of the need for vulnerability remediation
questions.explanation: Automated security checks reduce manual effort and human error while applying consistent security controls across builds.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the DevSecOps approach presented in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Security is an activity performed exclusively after deployment
questions.option_b: Security is continuously integrated into the software delivery process
questions.option_c: Security responsibilities belong only to infrastructure administrators
questions.option_d: Security testing should be separated from development and operations
questions.explanation: DevSecOps integrates security throughout development, testing, deployment, and runtime monitoring rather than treating it as a final-stage activity.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Static Application Security Testing (SAST)?
questions.option_a: To analyze running applications by simulating external attacks
questions.option_b: To analyze source code or compiled code without executing the application
questions.option_c: To monitor network traffic after production deployment
questions.option_d: To identify only vulnerabilities in third-party packages
questions.explanation: SAST examines source code or compiled code without executing the application to identify potential security weaknesses.

questions.question: Which vulnerability can be identified by SAST according to the lecture?
questions.option_a: Hardcoded credentials
questions.option_b: Physical server theft
questions.option_c: Unauthorized access to a data center
questions.option_d: Network cable damage
questions.explanation: SAST can identify hardcoded credentials, SQL injection risks, weak cryptography, insecure functions, and input validation issues.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a SAST tool?
questions.option_a: OWASP ZAP
questions.option_b: Semgrep
questions.option_d: Dependabot
questions.explanation: Semgrep is identified as a SAST tool. OWASP ZAP is used for DAST, TruffleHog for secret scanning, and Dependabot for dependency-related security.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Software Composition Analysis (SCA)?
questions.option_a: To analyze application behavior during runtime
questions.option_b: To identify vulnerabilities and risks in third-party dependencies
questions.option_c: To detect unauthorized changes in production databases
questions.option_d: To analyze source-code formatting
questions.explanation: SCA examines third-party libraries and dependencies to identify known vulnerabilities, outdated packages, licensing information, and dependency relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical SCA check?
questions.option_a: Dependency versions
questions.option_b: Known vulnerabilities
questions.option_d: Live user authentication behavior
questions.explanation: SCA examines software dependencies, including versions, vulnerabilities, licenses, and dependency relationships. Live authentication behavior is more relevant to application security testing.

questions.question: Which tool is identified in the lecture as an example of SCA?
questions.option_a: Checkmarx
questions.option_b: OWASP ZAP
questions.option_d: Gitleaks
questions.explanation: OWASP Dependency-Check is an SCA tool that helps identify known vulnerabilities in application dependencies.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of secret scanning?
questions.option_a: To identify outdated operating systems
questions.option_b: To detect sensitive credentials accidentally exposed in source-code repositories
questions.option_c: To identify SQL injection vulnerabilities in running applications
questions.option_d: To validate container networking configurations
questions.explanation: Secret scanning identifies exposed sensitive information such as AWS access keys, API tokens, database passwords, and private keys.

questions.question: A developer accidentally commits an AWS access key to a public Git repository. Which action is the most appropriate immediate response?
questions.option_a: Rename the repository and continue development
questions.option_b: Delete the local copy of the repository only
questions.option_c: Rotate the exposed credential immediately and investigate the exposure
questions.option_d: Wait for the next scheduled security audit
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends immediately rotating exposed credentials. Removing the visible secret alone does not invalidate a potentially compromised credential.

questions.question: Which tool is specifically identified as an example of secret scanning?
questions.option_a: Gitleaks
questions.option_b: Checkov
questions.option_d: OWASP ZAP
questions.explanation: Gitleaks is identified as a secret-scanning tool. It helps detect exposed credentials in repositories.

questions.question: What distinguishes Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) from SAST?
questions.option_a: DAST analyzes source code without execution, while SAST requires a running application
questions.option_b: DAST tests a running application externally, while SAST analyzes code without executing the application
questions.option_d: DAST only analyzes Dockerfiles, while SAST analyzes network configurations
questions.explanation: DAST tests a running application from the outside, whereas SAST analyzes source or compiled code without executing the application.

questions.question: Which vulnerability is particularly relevant to DAST testing?
questions.option_a: Cross-Site Scripting in a running web application
questions.option_b: An outdated package version in a dependency manifest
questions.option_c: A hardcoded API key in source code
questions.option_d: An unencrypted Terraform storage resource
questions.explanation: DAST can identify runtime web application vulnerabilities such as Cross-Site Scripting, SQL injection, authentication weaknesses, and session management problems.

questions.question: Which tool is identified in the lecture as an example of DAST?
questions.option_a: Semgrep
questions.option_b: Gitleaks
questions.option_d: Dependabot
questions.explanation: OWASP ZAP is identified as an example of Dynamic Application Security Testing.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security scanning?
questions.option_a: To identify security misconfigurations in infrastructure configuration files
questions.option_b: To execute application unit tests
questions.option_d: To identify formatting problems in application source code
questions.explanation: IaC scanning examines infrastructure definitions, such as Terraform and CloudFormation files, to identify insecure configurations before deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an IaC security issue?
questions.option_a: A missing unit test
questions.option_b: A public storage resource that should be private
questions.option_d: A hardcoded password in application source code
questions.explanation: Public storage, open firewall rules, excessive permissions, and unencrypted resources are examples of IaC misconfigurations.

questions.question: Which tool is identified as an example of IaC security scanning?
questions.option_a: Checkov
questions.option_b: TruffleHog
questions.option_d: Fortify
questions.explanation: Checkov is an IaC security scanning tool. The lecture also identifies tfsec and KICS.

questions.question: Which CI/CD stage is primarily associated with Software Composition Analysis in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Runtime
questions.option_b: Dependencies
questions.option_d: Infrastructure provisioning
questions.explanation: The lecture associates SCA with the Dependencies stage, where third-party libraries and packages are analyzed.

questions.question: Which security activity is associated with the runtime stage of the CI/CD security model?
questions.option_a: Secret scanning
questions.option_b: SAST
questions.option_d: Infrastructure as Code scanning
questions.explanation: Runtime security focuses on monitoring deployed systems and detecting potential threats during operation.

questions.question: Which security activity is most directly associated with the deployment stage?
questions.option_a: Policy checks
questions.option_b: Source-code compilation
questions.option_d: Unit testing
questions.explanation: The lecture associates deployment with policy checks to ensure that deployment conditions and security requirements are satisfied.

questions.question: A development team wants to detect weak cryptographic functions before running the application. Which security technique should they use?
questions.option_a: DAST
questions.option_b: SAST
questions.option_d: Artifact repository scanning
questions.explanation: SAST analyzes code without executing the application and can identify weak cryptography and insecure function usage.

questions.question: A company wants to discover whether its application uses a vulnerable version of the Requests Python library. Which security activity is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: SCA
questions.option_b: DAST
questions.option_d: Runtime threat detection
questions.explanation: SCA examines dependency versions and known vulnerabilities in third-party libraries such as Requests.

questions.question: A security engineer wants to test whether an application has weak session management by interacting with its running web interface. Which technique should be selected?
questions.option_a: SAST
questions.option_b: SCA
questions.option_d: IaC scanning
questions.explanation: DAST tests running applications externally and can identify authentication weaknesses and session management problems.

questions.question: What is the purpose of scanning infrastructure configuration before provisioning resources?
questions.option_a: To identify insecure configurations before they become deployed infrastructure
questions.option_b: To verify the application's user interface
questions.option_d: To automatically rotate every application dependency
questions.explanation: IaC scanning identifies misconfigurations such as open firewall rules and excessive permissions before infrastructure is provisioned.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of container image scanning in a CI/CD pipeline?
questions.option_a: To verify that developers have completed their code reviews
questions.option_b: To identify vulnerabilities and security issues in container images before deployment
questions.option_d: To automatically increase container resource allocation
questions.explanation: Container image scanning examines images for vulnerabilities, dependency risks, exposed secrets, and other security issues before deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a security check specifically mentioned for container images?
questions.option_a: Verify base images
questions.option_b: Check employee attendance
questions.option_d: Measure website search rankings
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies base-image verification as one of the security checks performed during container security validation.

questions.question: What does SBOM stand for?
questions.option_a: Secure Build Operation Management
questions.option_b: Software Bill of Materials
questions.option_d: Software Binary Optimization Mechanism
questions.explanation: SBOM stands for Software Bill of Materials. The lecture identifies SBOM generation as a container and software supply-chain security activity.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of generating an SBOM?
questions.option_a: To provide visibility into the software components included in an application or artifact
questions.option_b: To replace all application security testing
questions.option_c: To automatically deploy an application to production
questions.option_d: To encrypt every file in a container image
questions.explanation: An SBOM documents software components and helps organizations understand the components included in their software supply chain.

questions.question: Why should container images be signed?
questions.option_a: To increase the number of packages inside the image
questions.option_b: To provide a means of verifying image authenticity and integrity
questions.option_c: To eliminate the need for container registries
questions.option_d: To automatically patch all vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Image signing supports verification that an image is authentic and has not been modified without authorization.

questions.question: What should happen when a container image scan identifies a critical vulnerability under the example pipeline policy?
questions.option_a: The image should automatically be deployed
questions.option_b: The security scan should be ignored
questions.option_c: The pipeline should fail and deployment should be blocked
questions.option_d: Only the image name should be changed
questions.explanation: The lecture illustrates that a critical vulnerability can cause the pipeline to fail and prevent the vulnerable image from reaching production.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a container security check in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Scanning image vulnerabilities
questions.option_b: Detecting secrets
questions.option_d: Performing employee background verification
questions.explanation: Container security checks include vulnerability scanning, dependency scanning, secret detection, base-image verification, Dockerfile checks, SBOM generation, and signature verification.

questions.question: Which sequence best represents the container security process shown in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Code → Build Image → Image Scan → Vulnerability Check → Image Signing → Registry → Deployment
questions.option_b: Code → Deployment → Registry → Image Signing → Build Image
questions.option_c: Image Scan → Code → Production → Build Image → Registry
questions.option_d: Code → Image Signing → Deployment → Build Image → Vulnerability Check
questions.explanation: The presented process builds the container image, scans it, evaluates vulnerabilities, signs the image, stores it in a registry, and then proceeds toward deployment.

questions.question: What is a security gate in a CI/CD pipeline?
questions.option_a: A physical security device protecting a development office
questions.option_b: An automated condition determining whether a build can proceed to the next pipeline stage
questions.option_c: A manual process for creating source-code repositories
questions.option_d: A mechanism for increasing application execution speed
questions.explanation: A security gate evaluates automated conditions and determines whether the build is allowed to continue through the pipeline.

questions.question: Which condition is included in the example security gate policy from the lecture?
questions.option_a: Allow unlimited critical vulnerabilities
questions.option_b: Allow exposed secrets if the application passes unit tests
questions.option_d: Allow all high-risk IaC misconfigurations
questions.explanation: The example policy requires no critical vulnerabilities, no exposed secrets, a maximum of five medium vulnerabilities, and no high-risk IaC misconfigurations.

questions.question: Under the example security gate policy, how many medium vulnerabilities are permitted at most?
questions.option_a: Zero
questions.option_b: Three
questions.option_d: Ten
questions.explanation: The lecture's example policy allows a maximum of five medium vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What happens when a build fails a security gate?
questions.option_a: It automatically skips all remaining security checks and deploys
questions.option_b: It is stopped from proceeding to deployment
questions.option_c: It is automatically signed as a trusted artifact
questions.option_d: It is transferred directly to runtime monitoring
questions.explanation: A failed security gate prevents the build from proceeding to the next stage, including deployment when the failed gate precedes deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes automated compliance checking?
questions.option_a: Checking software against defined security policies automatically
questions.option_b: Manually inspecting application screenshots
questions.option_d: Automatically accepting every deployment
questions.explanation: Automated compliance checking evaluates configurations and systems against established security policies.

questions.question: Which activity is performed when every code commit is automatically analyzed for security weaknesses?
questions.option_a: Automated code scanning
questions.option_b: Manual artifact approval
questions.option_d: Infrastructure provisioning
questions.explanation: Automated code scanning checks code changes for security issues whenever commits are introduced.

questions.question: When should automated container scanning ideally occur according to the lecture?
questions.option_a: Only after the application has been running in production for several months
questions.option_b: Before container images are deployed
questions.option_c: Only when a customer reports a vulnerability
questions.option_d: Before developers write source code
questions.explanation: The lecture specifies that container images should be scanned before deployment to prevent vulnerable images from reaching production.

questions.question: Which security threat is associated with compromised developer credentials?
questions.option_a: An attacker may gain unauthorized access to development resources
questions.option_b: An application automatically loses its database schema
questions.option_c: A container image automatically becomes smaller
questions.option_d: The CI pipeline automatically becomes compliant
questions.explanation: Compromised developer credentials can allow attackers to access repositories and development systems, potentially enabling malicious changes.

questions.question: Which control is specifically recommended to protect against compromised developer credentials?
questions.option_a: Disable all code reviews
questions.option_b: Strong authentication and MFA
questions.option_d: Allow unrestricted repository access
questions.explanation: Strong authentication and multi-factor authentication reduce the risk of unauthorized access through compromised credentials.

questions.question: Which control helps reduce the risk of unauthorized pipeline modifications?
questions.option_a: Protected branches
questions.option_b: Publicly exposing CI/CD tokens
questions.option_d: Allowing all users to modify pipeline configurations
questions.explanation: Protected branches help prevent unauthorized modifications to important code branches and pipeline-related changes.

questions.question: Which security measure is recommended for protecting CI/CD artifacts?
questions.option_a: Artifact signing
questions.option_b: Disabling integrity verification
questions.option_d: Removing artifact version history
questions.explanation: Artifact signing provides a way to verify artifact authenticity and integrity before deployment.

questions.question: Why are secure build agents important?
questions.option_a: They reduce the need for software dependencies
questions.option_b: They help protect the build environment from compromise
questions.option_c: They automatically guarantee that application code is vulnerability-free
questions.option_d: They eliminate the need for repository authentication
questions.explanation: Secure build agents help protect the build infrastructure, which is a valuable target for attackers attempting to compromise software artifacts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a CI/CD pipeline security threat identified in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Malicious code commits
questions.option_b: Automatic unit test execution
questions.option_d: Dependency vulnerability scanning
questions.explanation: Malicious code commits are a pipeline security threat because attackers or malicious insiders may introduce harmful changes into the software.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of audit logging in CI/CD security?
questions.option_a: To hide unauthorized pipeline changes
questions.option_b: To maintain records that support tracking and investigating activities
questions.option_d: To eliminate the need for access control
questions.explanation: Audit logging records activities and changes, supporting accountability, investigation, and detection of suspicious pipeline behavior.

questions.question: Why is software supply-chain security important?
questions.option_a: Applications are built exclusively from internally written code
questions.option_b: Modern applications depend on external components that may introduce security risks
questions.option_d: Supply-chain attacks only affect physical manufacturing systems
questions.explanation: Modern software depends on libraries, container images, build tools, APIs, services, and package repositories, each of which may introduce security risks.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a potential supply-chain attack target?
questions.option_a: Open-source packages
questions.option_b: Only end-user monitors
questions.option_d: Only application documentation
questions.explanation: Attackers may compromise open-source packages, container images, build systems, CI/CD pipelines, and package repositories.

questions.question: What is the purpose of dependency version pinning?
questions.option_a: To allow dependencies to change versions without control
questions.option_b: To control which dependency versions are used during builds
questions.option_c: To eliminate the need for dependency scanning
questions.option_d: To automatically remove all third-party libraries
questions.explanation: Version pinning helps make dependency selection predictable and controlled, reducing risks associated with unexpected dependency changes.

questions.question: Which combination contains only supply-chain security measures listed in the lecture?
questions.option_a: Dependency scanning, SBOM, trusted repositories, and image signing
questions.option_b: Disabling version history, anonymous access, and unrestricted permissions
questions.option_c: Removing dependency checks, disabling logging, and allowing unsigned images
questions.option_d: Manual compilation, public credentials, and unverified artifacts
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies dependency scanning, SBOM generation, trusted repositories, image signing, artifact verification, version pinning, and continuous monitoring as supply-chain security measures.

questions.question: What is a software artifact in the context of the lecture?
questions.option_a: A file produced during the software build process
questions.option_b: A physical server used exclusively for testing
questions.option_d: A network firewall rule
questions.explanation: Artifacts are files produced during builds, including executables, packages, container images, libraries, and deployment packages.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a software artifact?
questions.option_a: A compiled application package
questions.option_b: A developer's personal identification document
questions.option_d: A network cable
questions.explanation: Compiled application packages are build outputs and therefore qualify as software artifacts.

questions.question: Why should software artifacts be stored in trusted repositories?
questions.option_a: To make artifacts publicly modifiable
questions.option_b: To support secure storage and controlled access to build outputs
questions.option_c: To eliminate the need for deployment verification
questions.option_d: To allow anonymous replacement of application packages
questions.explanation: Trusted artifact repositories help securely store build outputs and control access to artifacts before deployment.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent unauthorized modification of stored artifacts?
questions.option_a: Allowing unrestricted write permissions
questions.option_b: Disabling artifact verification
questions.option_c: Controlling access and verifying artifact integrity
questions.option_d: Deleting all artifact version information
questions.explanation: Access control and integrity verification help prevent unauthorized modification and allow artifact authenticity to be checked.

questions.question: Why should artifact version history be maintained?
questions.option_a: To make it impossible to identify previous builds
questions.option_b: To preserve records of artifact versions and support traceability
questions.option_c: To allow old artifacts to overwrite new artifacts without approval
questions.option_d: To replace all security scanning activities
questions.explanation: Maintaining version history supports traceability and helps identify which artifact versions were produced, stored, and used.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the secure artifact management process?
questions.option_a: Artifacts are stored anywhere and deployed without verification
questions.option_b: Artifacts are securely stored, scanned, verified, signed, and protected against unauthorized modification
questions.option_c: Artifacts are deployed before they are generated
questions.option_d: Artifacts are modified directly in production without maintaining versions
questions.explanation: Secure artifact management includes trusted repositories, access control, scanning, integrity verification, signing, version history, and protection against unauthorized modification.

questions.question: In the complete DevSecOps pipeline presented in the lecture, which activity follows source-code analysis and dependency scanning before the container build?
questions.option_a: Runtime monitoring
questions.option_b: Build
questions.option_d: Artifact deletion
questions.explanation: The pipeline places SAST and dependency scanning before the build stage, where the application is packaged.

questions.question: In the online shopping application worked example, which security activity checks Terraform configuration for misconfigurations?
questions.option_a: SAST
questions.option_b: SCA
questions.option_d: Secret rotation
questions.explanation: The worked example uses IaC scanning to examine Terraform configurations for security misconfigurations.

questions.question: In the online shopping application example, which activity ensures that only artifacts satisfying security policies can proceed?
questions.option_a: Security gate
questions.option_b: Dependency installation
questions.option_d: Runtime monitoring
questions.explanation: The security gate evaluates whether security policies are satisfied before the pipeline proceeds to deployment.

questions.question: Which activity is performed after deployment in the online shopping application example?
questions.option_a: SAST
questions.option_b: Runtime monitoring
questions.option_d: Container compilation
questions.explanation: The worked example performs continuous monitoring of the application and infrastructure after deployment.

questions.question: Which statement best represents the key message of the complete DevSecOps pipeline?
questions.option_a: Security should be performed only after all development activities are complete
questions.option_b: Security activities should be continuously integrated throughout the delivery pipeline
questions.option_c: Security scanning should replace all functional testing
questions.option_d: Only production systems require security controls
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes continuous integration of security activities rather than treating security as a final stage.

questions.question: A company discovers that its developers frequently introduce vulnerable third-party libraries. The vulnerabilities are usually identified only after deployment. Which change most directly addresses this problem?
questions.option_a: Introduce automated SCA checks when dependencies are added or updated
questions.option_b: Increase the frequency of production database backups
questions.option_c: Perform secret scanning only on deployment credentials
questions.option_d: Move all security testing to the runtime monitoring stage
questions.explanation: Early SCA checks identify vulnerable dependencies during development, demonstrating Shift-Left Security and reducing late-stage remediation.

questions.question: A security team must identify SQL injection vulnerabilities in both source code and a running web application. Which combination of techniques is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: SCA and secret scanning
questions.option_b: SAST and DAST
questions.option_d: SBOM generation and artifact versioning
questions.explanation: SAST can identify potential SQL injection weaknesses through code analysis, while DAST tests the running application externally to identify exploitable behavior.

questions.question: A developer commits an API token into a repository. The pipeline detects it, but the developer removes the token from the latest commit and immediately retries the build. What is the most important additional security action?
questions.option_a: Generate a new container image without changing the credential
questions.option_b: Rotate or revoke the exposed token because it may already have been compromised
questions.option_c: Disable secret scanning for future commits
questions.option_d: Move the token into a different source-code file
questions.explanation: Removing a secret from the latest commit does not guarantee that it was never accessed. The exposed credential must be rotated or revoked.

questions.question: A company uses SAST, SCA, DAST, and IaC scanning but performs all four checks immediately before production deployment. Which principle is it failing to implement effectively?
questions.option_a: Artifact versioning
questions.option_b: Shift-Left Security
questions.option_d: Container portability
questions.explanation: Although the company uses appropriate security techniques, delaying all checks until the final stage contradicts Shift-Left Security, which encourages earlier security activities.

questions.question: A container image passes application tests but contains a known critical vulnerability in one of its underlying packages. The organization's policy prohibits critical vulnerabilities. What should the CI/CD pipeline do?
questions.option_a: Deploy the image because functional tests passed
questions.option_b: Ignore the vulnerability because it exists in the base image
questions.option_c: Fail the security gate and block deployment
questions.option_d: Generate an SBOM and automatically approve the image
questions.explanation: Functional testing does not override security policies. A critical vulnerability violates the example security gate policy and should block deployment.

questions.question: An organization wants to establish which third-party libraries are included in a container image so that it can assess the impact of newly discovered vulnerabilities. Which security measure is most useful?
questions.option_a: SBOM generation
questions.option_b: Protected branches
questions.option_d: Session management testing
questions.explanation: An SBOM provides visibility into software components, helping organizations identify whether newly discovered vulnerabilities affect their software.

questions.question: A company scans its source code for hardcoded credentials but does not scan its Git repository for exposed API tokens in configuration files or historical commits. Which security activity should be strengthened?
questions.option_a: Secret scanning
questions.option_b: DAST
questions.option_d: Runtime monitoring
questions.explanation: Secret scanning is specifically intended to identify sensitive credentials exposed in repositories. It complements SAST rather than being replaced by it.

questions.question: A developer updates a dependency manifest to use the latest version of a third-party package. However, the package repository has been compromised and the new version contains malicious code. Which combination of measures would best help reduce this supply-chain risk?
questions.option_a: Trusted repositories, dependency scanning, version pinning, and artifact verification
questions.option_b: Disabling dependency scanning and allowing automatic updates
questions.option_c: Using only DAST and disabling source-code reviews
questions.option_d: Removing runtime monitoring and increasing deployment frequency
questions.explanation: Trusted repositories, dependency scanning, controlled versions, and artifact verification provide complementary protections against compromised dependencies and malicious software components.

questions.question: A CI/CD pipeline allows every developer to modify deployment configurations and pipeline credentials. An attacker compromises one developer account and changes the pipeline to deploy malicious code. Which combination of controls most directly addresses this attack?
questions.option_a: Protected branches, MFA, least privilege, and audit logging
questions.option_b: SBOM generation, image compression, and unit testing
questions.option_c: DAST, dependency version updates, and application caching
questions.option_d: Runtime monitoring alone
questions.explanation: MFA reduces credential compromise risk, least privilege limits access, protected branches restrict unauthorized modifications, and audit logs support investigation.

questions.question: A company uses a secure artifact repository, but deployment servers download artifacts without verifying their signatures or integrity. What is the primary remaining risk?
questions.option_a: The application cannot execute unit tests
questions.option_b: A modified or substituted artifact could be deployed without being detected
questions.option_c: The repository cannot store multiple versions
questions.option_d: The source-code repository will automatically become public
questions.explanation: Secure storage alone does not guarantee that the artifact received by a deployment system is authentic and unchanged. Signature and integrity verification are also necessary.

questions.question: An infrastructure team uses Terraform to provision cloud storage. The configuration accidentally makes a storage resource publicly accessible. Which action provides the earliest opportunity to prevent this misconfiguration?
questions.option_a: Use IaC scanning before infrastructure deployment
questions.option_b: Use DAST after users access the storage resource
questions.option_d: Use secret scanning on application source code
questions.explanation: IaC scanning can identify public storage configurations before resources are provisioned, preventing the misconfiguration from reaching the deployed environment.

questions.question: A company performs container vulnerability scanning and generates an SBOM but does not verify the authenticity of images before deployment. Which security requirement is missing?
questions.option_a: Image signature verification
questions.option_b: Dependency version discovery
questions.option_d: SBOM generation
questions.explanation: Image scanning and SBOM generation provide vulnerability and component visibility, but signature verification is separately needed to establish image authenticity and integrity.

questions.question: A pipeline uses the following security policy: zero critical vulnerabilities, no exposed secrets, no high-risk IaC misconfigurations, and a maximum of five medium vulnerabilities. A build contains zero critical vulnerabilities, one exposed API key, zero high-risk IaC issues, and three medium vulnerabilities. What should happen?
questions.option_a: Pass because the number of medium vulnerabilities is below five
questions.option_b: Pass because no critical vulnerabilities exist
questions.option_c: Fail because the exposed API key violates the security policy
questions.option_d: Pass because only production credentials need to be checked
questions.explanation: Every security gate condition must be satisfied. Even though the other conditions pass, the exposed API key violates the explicit no-exposed-secrets requirement.

questions.question: A build has two critical vulnerabilities, no exposed secrets, four medium vulnerabilities, and no high-risk IaC misconfigurations. According to the example policy, what is the correct decision?
questions.option_a: Pass because the number of medium vulnerabilities is acceptable
questions.option_b: Fail because critical vulnerabilities are prohibited
questions.option_c: Pass because no secrets were exposed
questions.option_d: Pass if the image has been signed
questions.explanation: The policy explicitly prohibits critical vulnerabilities. Passing other conditions or signing the image does not override this requirement.

questions.question: A company wants to detect authentication and session management weaknesses in its shopping application. It also wants to identify insecure functions in its source code. Which testing arrangement is correct?
questions.option_a: SAST for runtime authentication behavior and DAST for source-code analysis
questions.option_b: DAST for runtime authentication and session behavior, and SAST for insecure source-code functions
questions.option_d: IaC scanning for both activities
questions.explanation: DAST tests running applications and can identify authentication and session weaknesses. SAST analyzes source code and can identify insecure functions.

questions.question: A company uses an artifact repository with access controls and version history. An attacker compromises a build server and replaces a package with a malicious version before it is uploaded. Which additional measure is most directly useful for detecting unauthorized artifact modification?
questions.option_a: Artifact integrity verification and signing
questions.option_b: Increasing the number of application unit tests
questions.option_d: Allowing all developers to approve deployments
questions.explanation: Artifact integrity verification and signing help establish whether an artifact has been altered and whether it originates from a trusted source.

questions.question: A development team uses a vulnerable third-party library. The library is included in a container image, which is scanned only after production deployment. Which combination of improvements most directly applies Shift-Left Security?
questions.option_a: Perform SCA when dependencies are introduced and container scanning before deployment
questions.option_b: Perform runtime monitoring only after customer complaints
questions.option_c: Disable container scanning and depend on application availability tests
questions.option_d: Generate artifact version numbers without examining dependencies
questions.explanation: Early SCA detects vulnerable dependencies before the build progresses, while pre-deployment container scanning checks the packaged image before it reaches production.

questions.question: An attacker compromises a CI/CD token and uses it to access a build system. The attacker modifies a pipeline to upload a malicious container image to a registry. Which controls provide the most comprehensive defense against this scenario?
questions.option_a: Secret management, least privilege, secure build agents, artifact signing, and audit logging
questions.option_b: Application formatting, unit testing, and interface validation only
questions.option_c: Dependency version pinning without pipeline access controls
questions.option_d: DAST alone
questions.explanation: The attack targets credentials, pipeline infrastructure, and build artifacts. Protecting secrets, restricting privileges, securing build agents, signing artifacts, and logging activities address different parts of the attack.

questions.question: A team uses SAST and SCA successfully, but an attacker exploits a vulnerability in the deployed application that becomes visible only through its runtime behavior. Which security activity should complement the existing checks?
questions.option_a: DAST and runtime monitoring
questions.option_b: Artifact version history alone
questions.option_d: Dependency version pinning alone
questions.explanation: DAST tests running applications for externally observable vulnerabilities, while runtime monitoring helps detect threats after deployment. These complement SAST and SCA.

questions.question: An organization wants to prevent a compromised package from silently changing between builds. It also wants to know which software components were included in each released version. Which combination best supports these requirements?
questions.option_a: Version pinning and SBOM generation
questions.option_b: DAST and session management testing
questions.option_d: Runtime monitoring and firewall configuration only
questions.explanation: Version pinning controls which dependency versions are used, while SBOM generation records the software components included in a build.

questions.question: A company blocks deployment when a container vulnerability scan fails. However, the pipeline allows the same artifact to be replaced in the registry after approval without another verification. What is the most significant weakness?
questions.option_a: The pipeline lacks continuous unit testing
questions.option_b: The approved artifact could be modified or substituted after the security gate
questions.option_c: The company performs too many security checks
questions.option_d: The pipeline cannot generate source code
questions.explanation: A security gate only establishes that the evaluated artifact satisfied the policy at that point. Artifact signing, integrity verification, and access controls help ensure that the approved artifact is the one eventually deployed.

questions.question: A company wants to enforce that every build follows the same security requirements and that developers receive immediate feedback about security problems. Which approach best satisfies both objectives?
questions.option_a: Perform security audits manually once per year
questions.option_b: Integrate automated security scans and security gates into the CI/CD pipeline
questions.option_c: Perform security testing only after production incidents
questions.option_d: Allow individual developers to decide whether security checks are necessary
questions.explanation: Automated scans provide fast feedback, while security gates enforce consistent security requirements across builds.

questions.question: A software company uses third-party APIs, open-source libraries, container images, and external build tools. Which statement best describes its supply-chain security responsibility?
questions.option_a: It only needs to secure source code written by its own developers
questions.option_b: It must consider risks introduced by external components and services throughout the software supply chain
questions.option_c: It only needs to secure the production database
questions.option_d: It can trust every dependency because it comes from a public repository
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies libraries, container images, build tools, APIs, third-party services, and package repositories as potential supply-chain attack targets.

questions.question: A development organization has introduced automated code scanning, dependency scanning, container scanning, IaC scanning, and compliance checks. Which major DevSecOps benefit is most directly demonstrated?
questions.option_a: Security becomes a one-time activity
questions.option_b: Security controls are applied continuously and consistently throughout development and delivery
questions.option_c: All vulnerabilities are guaranteed to be eliminated
questions.option_d: Developers no longer need to understand security
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes continuous security integration, consistency, reduced human error, faster feedback, and shared responsibility across development, security, and operations.
